checks.s: Section 2 states that the guaranty covers both payment and performance of the Guaranteed Obligations.
Section 1 retains the defined term “Excluded Swap Obligations.”
The definition of Guaranteed Obligations excludes swap obligations for which the Guarantor is not an “eligible contract participant” under the Commodity Exchange Act.
Section 5 does not give the Guarantor an operative right to terminate the guaranty for future obligations on 90 calendar days’ prior written notice or any other notice period.
Section 10 contains the mutual jury trial waiver.
Section 4 does not limit reinstatement to payments actually received by the Administrative Agent directly from the Guarantor, excluding payments from the Borrower or collateral proceeds.

Section 4 provides for reinstatement if any payment on the Guaranteed Obligations is rescinded or must be returned, regardless of its source, including payments from the Borrower or collateral proceeds.
Section 3 does not make subrogation effective immediately upon any payment and instead subordinates the Guarantor’s subrogation, contribution, and reimbursement rights against the Borrower.
Section 3 bars the Guarantor from exercising subrogation rights until all Guaranteed Obligations have been indefeasibly paid in full.
Section 3 bars the Guarantor from exercising subrogation rights until all commitments under the Credit Agreement have been terminated.
The cover note identifies Priya Narayan of Whitfield Crane & Sadler LLP as its sender or author.
The cover note identifies Thomas Kuo of Marchetti DeLuca LLP as its primary addressee.
The cover note lists Marcus Ellingham of Cascadia National Bank as a cc recipient.
The cover note lists Diana Chow of Terraverde Group, Inc. as a cc recipient.
Section 2 does not make enforceability of the guaranty subject to a five (5) business-day waiting period after written demand is delivered to the Guarantor, or a comparable waiting period.
Section 3 states that the Guarantor waives any right to require the Administrative Agent to proceed first against the Borrower or any collateral before enforcing the guaranty.
Section 3 states that the Guarantor waives any defense arising from the Administrative Agent’s election of remedies.
Section 11 does not require the Guarantor’s written consent for an amendment, modification, or waiver of the Guaranty Agreement.
Section 11 provides that amendments, modifications, or waivers of the Guaranty Agreement require only the consent of the Administrative Agent acting at the direction of the Required Lenders.
Section 2 accepts the concept of a fraudulent-conveyance savings clause using revised or market-standard savings-clause language.
Section 2 proposes an alternative formulation of the fraudulent-conveyance savings clause.
Section 8 accepts or proposes a de minimis dollar-threshold carve-out from the intercompany-debt subordination provision.
Section 8 does not limit intercompany-debt subordination to periods during which an Event of Default under the Credit Agreement is continuing.
Section 3 states that the Guarantor waives any defense based on or arising from any applicable statute of limitations.
The definition of Guaranteed Obligations in Section 1 does not exclude obligations arising after an acceleration of which the Guarantor did not receive notice.
The Guaranty Agreement does not condition enforceability on delivery of a customary enforceability opinion from the Guarantor’s Delaware counsel.
The cover note gives a reason for the agent’s position that the guaranty should cover both payment and performance.

The cover note gives a reason for the agent’s position on the Section 3 suretyship waivers, including the waiver of marshaling, the election-of-remedies defense, or the statute-of-limitations defense.
The cover note explains why reinstatement under Section 4 must apply regardless of the source of a clawed-back payment.
The cover note gives a reason for rejecting the Guarantor’s proposed right to terminate the guaranty for future obligations upon 90 calendar days’ notice.
The cover note gives a reason for the agent’s position on Section 8 intercompany-debt subordination, including the proposed threshold or the proposed Event of Default limitation.
The cover note gives a reason for restoring the jury trial waiver deleted by the Guarantor’s counsel from Section 10.
The cover note organizes its substantive issues by section reference, issue category, or topical heading.
